# Results — Study 726 (Chicken-Wing-Index): does the Super Bowl give Wingstop a tradable calendar? 2015–2026

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Monthly returns of **Wingstop (WING)**,
the **S&P 500 ETF (SPY**, the market leg for the alpha regression**)** and the **13-week T-bill**
(^IRX, the cash leg), built from daily closes resampled to month-end on a verified hole-free grid:
2015-07 → 2026-05, **131 months** (only **11 completed Januaries**). As-of 2026-06-01; inputs
fingerprint `5742cb7dc999`. WING is auto-adjusted but pays no dividend → effectively price-only; SPY is
total-return-ish (dividends reinvested). Labeled accordingly.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `NONE` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · "Super Bowl bump"? `BUSTED`

The folklore is delicious: Americans eat ~1.4 billion wings on Super Bowl Sunday, so wing demand should
spike into the early-February game and Wingstop — the pure-play wing chain — should rally into it. The
tape says the "wing window" is a **data-snooping mirage** dressed up as a calendar.

**January alone looks real** — WING's average January is **+7.20%/month, naive t = 2.52** — and that
single number is the entire steelman. But it does not survive contact with the thesis. The statistic that
actually encodes the claim — *does the Super-Bowl run-up window beat every other month?* — is a spread of
**+5.10%/month with Welch t = 1.62**, and its block-bootstrap 95% CI is **[−0.31%, +10.36%]**, straddling
zero. **February — the actual Super Bowl month — is *negative* (−2.01%)**, the opposite of what a
demand-into-the-game story predicts (Feb-vs-rest t = −1.33). And January is not even the best month: in a
12-month placebo, **off-thesis November ranks #1** (Sharpe 0.66, t = 2.70) with January #2 (0.63, t =
2.52) — exactly the pattern selection manufactures when you search twelve months for the biggest one
(Bonferroni for 12 tests needs |t| ≈ 3). The whole "wing season" (Dec–Jan) is t = 0.20. `NONE`.

## Data stamp

- **Series**: WING + SPY + ^IRX monthly, 2015-07 → 2026-05, **131 months** (11 Januaries), as-of
  2026-06-01, fingerprint `5742cb7dc999`
- **Construction**: daily closes resampled to month-end (last close of each calendar month). Grid asserted
  hole-free on every read by `fetch_data`. WING pays no dividend (auto-adjust ⇒ price-only in practice);
  SPY is dividend-reinvested (total-return-ish) — the two are used only for a same-month excess/alpha, so
  the mild mismatch is immaterial and labeled.

## Per-month WING statistics (one-sample t vs 0, n ≈ 11 each)

| Month | Mean | t (naive) | t (HAC) | n | Signal? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jan | +7.20% | +2.52 | +5.36 | 11 | Nominal only — one snooped month, on-thesis |
| Feb | −2.01% | −0.58 | −0.80 | 11 | **No — the game month is negative** |
| Mar | −3.51% | −0.78 | −0.81 | 11 | No |
| Apr | +9.39% | +1.83 | +2.54 | 11 | No |
| May | +1.86% | +0.53 | +0.61 | 11 | No |
| Jun | +6.02% | +2.25 | +2.56 | 10 | Nominal only, off-thesis |
| Jul | +8.58% | +1.25 | +1.63 | 11 | No |
| Aug | +2.42% | +0.53 | +0.50 | 11 | No |
| Sep | −3.49% | −1.00 | −1.04 | 11 | No |
| Oct | −4.51% | −1.05 | −1.14 | 11 | No |
| Nov | +9.97% | +2.70 | +2.95 | 11 | Nominal only, **off-thesis — and the strongest of all** |
| Dec | −1.29% | −0.49 | −0.55 | 11 | No |

Three months (Nov, Jan, Jun) clear a *naive* |t| ≥ 2; the largest is **November**, which has nothing to
do with wings. None clears the Bonferroni threshold for 12 tests (α = 0.05/12 ≈ 0.004 ⇒ |t| ≈ 3). The
HAC t is quoted for completeness but is **not trustworthy at n ≈ 11** — its long-run variance is estimated
on a handful of points; the honest inference is the Welch window test, the bootstrap CI and the placebo.

## The Super-Bowl window vs the rest of the year (the headline)

| | Mean monthly return | n |
|---|---|---|
| Super-Bowl run-up window (January) | +7.20% | 11 |
| Every other month | +2.10% | 120 |
| **Spread** | **+5.10%** | — |
| **t-stat (Welch)** | **1.62** | — |
| **Block-bootstrap 95% CI** | **[−0.31%, +10.36%]** | 5000 resamples, 12-month blocks |
| February (the game month) vs rest | **−4.95%**, t = −1.33 | 11 |
| "Wing season" (Dec–Jan) vs rest | +0.51%, t = 0.20 | 22 |

The window's direction is nominally as folklore predicts, but the thesis-level test does **not** clear
|t| ≥ 2 and the CI straddles zero. The game month itself is negative. **The window is indistinguishable
from noise.**

## Is January just the market's January? (alpha vs SPY)

Regressing the 11 January WING returns on the same-month SPY returns: alpha **+5.69%/month, naive
t = 2.00**, beta **1.03**; mean WING-minus-SPY January excess **+5.73%**. SPY's own average January is
**+1.47%**. So part of the January pop is the well-documented turn-of-year / small-cap January effect, and
the WING-specific residual sits *exactly on* the |t| = 2 line — on 11 data points, with beta ≈ 1. That is
the definition of fragile: one more weak January and it crosses under. It cannot certify a Super-Bowl
effect; it cannot even cleanly separate WING from the calendar everybody already knows about.

## The 12-month placebo — January is not special

Long-one-month / cash-otherwise timer, excess-of-T-bill Sharpe, ranked:

| Rank | Month | Sharpe | t | On-thesis? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **November** | **0.66** | +2.70 | **No** |
| 2 | January | 0.63 | +2.52 | Yes |
| 3 | June | 0.57 | +2.25 | No |
| 4 | April | 0.50 | +1.83 | No |
| … | … | … | … | … |

If the Super Bowl drove the pattern, January would stand alone at the top. Instead an entirely off-thesis
month (November) beats it, with June close behind. This is what a 12-way search looks like: the winner is
a coin that came up heads, not a mechanism.

## The calendar timer vs buy-and-hold

Long WING in January, T-bill otherwise (calendar-known, no execution lag). Sharpe = excess of T-bill,
both legs. Net charges 10 bp one-way × NAV per leg (2 legs/yr).

| | CAGR | Sharpe (excess) | vol | max-DD |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super-Bowl timer (gross) | +9.0% | **0.63** | 0.11 | −11% |
| timer (net 10 bp/leg) | +8.7% | 0.61 | 0.11 | −11% |
| buy & hold WING | **+20.7%** | 0.57 | 0.49 | −63% |

Here is the trap the pitch relies on: the timer's Sharpe (0.63) is *nominally higher* than buy-and-hold's
(0.57). But that is a **de-risking illusion, not an edge** — the timer sits in T-bills eleven months a year,
so of course its volatility (11%) and drawdown (−11%) collapse. It does so by **forgoing more than half of
WING's compound return** (9.0% CAGR vs 20.7%). You are not harvesting a wing premium; you are declining to
own a great growth stock for eleven months and calling the reduced variance "risk-adjusted outperformance."
And the one month you *do* hold isn't even the best one (November's timer Sharpe is higher). Costs are an
afterthought — there is no genuine gross edge to defend.

## Sub-period — the window never clears the bar in either half

| Period | January mean | rest-of-year mean | window t | n_Jan |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2016–2020 | +7.30% | +3.69% | 0.74 | 5 |
| 2021–on | +7.12% | +1.10% | 1.32 | 6 |

Neither half produces a significant window spread. A five-January and a six-January sub-sample are far too
thin to certify a seasonal law, and neither tries to.

## The wholesale-wing-price proxy — supply shocks, not a calendar

The hardcoded, cited, **approximate** pre-Super-Bowl wholesale whole-wing price (US$/lb; a *labelled
proxy*, not a live feed, and **not tradable** — wings have no futures market) tells the same story from the
physical side. It was rangebound near **$1.5–1.9** through 2016–2020, spiked **+72% to a record ~$2.86/lb
into early 2021** (the pandemic wing shortage — wings briefly the priciest cut of the bird), then
**crashed −52.8% to ~$1.28 by 2023** as supply normalised. The price is driven by avian-flu and
supply-chain shocks, not by an annual Super-Bowl demand bump you could time.

## The honest takeaway

The chicken-wing trade has the most *fun* premise on the bench — a billion wings on one Sunday — and it
fails the same way every seasonal-mining story fails. One month (January) shows a naive t = 2.5, but it is
one snooped month of twelve, it is out-ranked by off-thesis November, February (the actual game) is
*negative*, the thesis-level window test is t = 1.62 with a CI straddling zero, the January "alpha" over
SPY sits exactly on the t = 2 line on 11 points and is half just the ordinary January effect, and the
calendar timer only "wins" on Sharpe by sitting in cash and forgoing WING's growth. `NONE` on the signal,
`MIRAGE` as a trade, Super-Bowl bump `BUSTED`.
